ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $BD$ bisects $\angle ABC$, $CD \perp BD$ with the foot of the perpendicular being D, and E is the midpoint of $AC$. If $AB=30$, $BC=18$, what is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure:\\
Extend CD to intersect AB at F.\\
In $\triangle BDC$ and $\triangle BDF$, we have\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle DBC=\angle DBF\\
BD=BD\\
\angle BDC=\angle BDF=90^\circ
\end{array}\right.$\\
$\therefore \triangle BDC \cong \triangle BDF$ (ASA)\\
$\therefore BF=BC=18$, CD=DF\\
$\therefore AF=AB-BF=12$,\\
$\because E$ is the midpoint of AC,\\
$\therefore CE=EA$\\
$\because CD=DF$,\\
$\therefore DE=\frac{1}{2}AF=\boxed{6}.$

Extend line CD past D until it meets line AB at a new point F. ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure:\\
Extend CD to intersect AB at F.\\
In $\triangle BDC$ and $\triangle BDF$, we have\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle DBC=\angle DBF\\
BD=BD\\
\angle BDC=\angle BDF=90^\circ
\end{array}\right.$\\
$\therefore \triangle BDC \cong \triangle BDF$ (ASA)\\
$\therefore BF=BC=18$, CD=DF\\
$\therefore AF=AB-BF=12$,\\
$\because E$ is the midpoint of AC,\\
$\therefore CE=EA$\\
$\because CD=DF$,\\
$\therefore DE=\frac{1}{2}AF=\boxed{6}.$
